correctness.rationale: If commuting rank-one operators have a nonzero common product, their images coincide; both operators kill that line by square-zero, contradicting the nonzero product. In a nonempty clique each covector therefore kills the image span U, giving containment in C(U). The images and covectors of the full C(U) span U and U⊥ respectively, so no new vertex can commute with all its members, and U is recovered from the clique. Dividing the nonzero vector/covector factor count by q−1 gives the sizes; minimizing q^r+q^(n−r) gives exactly the stated middle ranks. For the polynomial use the unique image/covector span pair (U,W), with W≤U⊥. The number of pairs is [n choose r]_q[n−r choose s]_q. In fixed smaller spans of dimensions i,j all subsets contribute (1+z)^((q^i−1)(q^j−1)/(q−1)); inversion on the product of the two subspace lattices isolates the exact spans with the displayed coefficients. The empty clique is included separately. The argument uses finite-field algebra in every characteristic. Fresh direct matrix-product enumeration over F₂ gives coefficients (1,21,42,14) at n=3 and (1,105,1260,3780,5460,5040,3150,1290,315,35) at n=4, including the empty clique.
residual_risks: The fresh computation covers only two binary cases. The proof, not this check or the frozen prime-field output, establishes all prime powers.

originality.rationale: The assigned mathematical claims are demonstrably covered in the present catalog by a distinct indexed record, not merely a similar title or a reference to the identical frozen item. The November 1 record proves the same maximal-clique classification and computes every coefficient of the same clique polynomial. Its one-span tuple formula becomes the subset formula by Stirling inversion; the frozen two-span version refines intermediate summands without adding a different final invariant. The November 2 double-flag formula also covers that intermediate refinement by specializing all ranks to one. These findings are about equivalent indexed coverage, not historical priority: the matching records have later catalog dates than the assigned source, and this audit does not claim they anticipated it.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a natural classification question for an incidence graph and gives a uniform size distribution for all cliques, beyond local graph statistics. Distinguishing true matrix vertices from scalar classes and using exact spans to avoid overcounting makes it useful as a mathematical description of the graph. This assessment of the question and complete answer does not give credit for novelty over the verified catalog coverage.
residual_risks: There is no demonstrated new downstream consequence or algorithmic advantage of the alternative formula over the matching indexed results.
